svg.aria-label: Pancreatic lipase anchored by colipase at the lipid droplet surface, with the enzymes of luminal lipid digestion and their products
svg.text: Colipase anchors lipase to a bile-salt-coated surface
lipid droplet core
triacylglycerol
lipase
colipase
Bile salts cover the surface and repel lipase.
Colipase binds the surface and binds lipase, in
a 1:1 complex, restoring access to the esters.
Procolipase is secreted inactive and is cut by
trypsin in the duodenum.
Enzymes of luminal lipid digestion
Lingual and gastric lipase
acid-stable; act on short- and medium-chain triacylglycerol
Pancreatic lipase + colipase
triacylglycerol at sn-1 and sn-3 to 2-monoacylglycerol + 2 free fatty acids
Cholesterol esterase (carboxyl ester lipase)
cholesteryl ester to cholesterol + fatty acid; also hydrolyses 2-MAG
Phospholipase A2 (secreted as proenzyme, cut by trypsin)
phospholipid at sn-2 to lysophospholipid + fatty acid; needs Ca2+
Secretion is driven by cholecystokinin; bicarbonate from secretin raises pH to the optimum of about 6-8.
Net products delivered to the micelle
2-monoacylglycerol · free fatty acids · cholesterol · lysophospholipid
plus the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K released from the fat phase
Short- and medium-chain fatty acids need neither micelles nor chylomicrons.
